notes: This minor release requires Bifrost 0.15.1 or later, as rules 0.10.0 did, and depends exactly on bifrost.public.packs 0.11.0. It adds eight policies to bifrost.security 2.3.0, changes the severity of 61 CodeQL-parity quality policies, and changes no policy ID. New in bifrost.security: two default-on C# taint policies, bifrost.security.csharp.regex-pattern-injection (CVE-2019-0820) and bifrost.security.csharp.dataset-read-xml-external-location (CVE-2020-1147) (#319), and six opt-in policies: bifrost.security.go.network-read-all-unbounded (CVE-2022-30631; reports a network connection read to EOF by io.ReadAll or io.Copy with or without gzip decompression, and io.LimitReader sanitizes) (#320); bifrost.security.java.objectinputstream-read-without-filter (CVE-2026-41586; typestate) (#324); bifrost.security.python.process-input-to-urlopen and bifrost.security.python.process-input-to-webbrowser-open (#323); and bifrost.security.javascript.process-input-to-fs-write-path and bifrost.security.javascript.process-input-to-legacy-url-parse (#317). Their required capabilities are all advertised by Bifrost 0.15.1, and every locked policy identity verifies on that release. Known limits: the two C# policies use the BCL models bifrost.dotnet.system-text-regularexpressions-csharp and bifrost.dotnet.system-data-csharp, and the two JavaScript policies use the Node path, url and fs models, which are source-only and not in packs 0.11.0, so without a model the two C# policies report not_run, and the two JavaScript policies report no findings and an inconclusive run, in a check on Bifrost 0.15.1 with the fixture models removed. The Java policy reports every finding as possible and its runs as inconclusive on 0.15.1 (bifrost-dev#10001). The two Python policies are opt-in because a process input read after any modeled call is not selected (bifrost-dev#9999) and a urlopen keyword argument fails the run (bifrost-dev#9991). The Go policy needs the packs 0.11.0 io, gzip and net models, which activate only on a Go toolchain of 1.26.0 or later. Severity changes, with detection logic unchanged (#330, #331): 51 policies that upstream CodeQL rates as recommendations move from warning to note (bifrost.csharp-codeql-quality 8, bifrost.java-codeql-quality 15, bifrost.javascript-codeql-quality 3, bifrost.python-codeql-quality 25), so a gate set to fail on warning no longer fails on them; and 10 policies that upstream rates as errors move from warning to error (bifrost.csharp-codeql-quality recursive-equals-call, self-assignment and stringbuilder-initialized-with-character, and seven in bifrost.python-codeql-quality), so a gate set to fail on error now fails on them. These four packs move to bifrost.csharp-codeql-quality 0.5.1, bifrost.java-codeql-quality 0.1.2, bifrost.javascript-codeql-quality 0.1.2 and bifrost.python-codeql-quality 0.1.2. The staged bifrost.rust-codeql-security endpoint catalogs (#326) are not policies and enable nothing. All other policies, IDs and consumer requirements are unchanged from rules 0.10.0. This release does not qualify the full policy set or imply complete analysis.
